author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence’s police union is seeking clarity about its future relationship with Democratic mayoral nominee David Morales after his primary victory over incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley. Fraternal Order of Police President Michael Imondi said the union and nominee had not yet spoken and raised questions about staffing, resources and support for officers.

Imondi told NBC 10 that nearly 100 officers could leave the department during the next year. That figure is the union president’s estimate, not an announced departure count. The department currently has about 450 officers, according to the report, making retention and response capacity central concerns as city leadership prepares for a possible transition.

Morales said he wants rank-and-file officers to know that he would listen to their concerns and work with them on community safety. He also said he looked forward to a conversation with police leadership. During the campaign, Morales stepped back from earlier calls to defund the police. The nomination does not decide the office: Morales will face Republican Dave Talan in the November general election. A meeting between the nominee and union would be the first step toward defining how they might work together.
dek: The union president raised staffing concerns while Democratic nominee David Morales said he wants to listen to officers and work with them.
headline: Providence police union seeks dialogue with Morales after primary win
